as_sent.description:
Send the stored bytes exactly as they were sent, uncorrected (plan
6.2). Not with edits or `--request`.

body.description: A new body: text, `@FILE` (an absolute path) or `-` (standard input).

dry_run.description:
Print the request that would be sent, the scope verdict and the units
needed against units left; send nothing.

flow.description:
The flow to replay: an ID, `@last`, `@-n` or `@sel`. Not with
`--macro` (the request is step N of the macro).

follow.description:
Follow up to this many redirects (0: none, at most 20). Each hop is
checked like the first request and spends a unit.

header.description:
A header, `'Name: value'`; replaces every header of that name,
`'Name:'` removes it. Repeatable.

macro.description:
Replay a step of this macro (its file name without `.toml`): the
steps before `--step` run fresh in the same job, their variables go
into the step, then the edits apply and it is sent. Needs `--step`.

raw_file.description:
Send the bytes of this file exactly, uncorrected, to the flow's
destination. Not with edits, `--request` or `--as-sent`.

request.description:
The whole edited request, start line, headers and body: a file or
`-` for standard input (the CLI reads it; over the control socket
this is the request text). Re-serialised with `Content-Length`
corrected; `--set`, `--header` and `--body` apply after it.

session.description:
`NAME`: send as that session. `anon`: send with no credentials
(Cookie, Authorization and every session's extra header names are
removed). `none`: no session, the flow as recorded, overriding the
project default. Without it the project default (`sessions use`) is
used, else none. Not with `--as-sent` or `--raw-file` (raw bytes go
as written).

set.description:
An edit of the request, `LOCATION:PATH=VALUE` (`json:items[0].qty=-1`).
Repeatable; the locations are listed in the description below.

step.description: With `--macro`: the step to replay, from 1.

times.description:
Send it this many times, one after another (1 to 100). Every unit is
reserved before the first is sent; each copy is a flow with the same
parent.

Advice.description:
One advice entry: a level, a short kebab-case `type` for programs to match
on, a message, and optionally the one command that follows it up.

command.description: The command that acts on this advice, if any.

message.description: One line for people. For `next`, the command itself.

AdviceLevel.description: How much an advice entry matters.

oneOf.description: Something to know or do next.
Something failed (a gate, a partial batch).

ErrorBody.description: The value under `error` in an error envelope. Published by `teapot schema`.

Exit.description: Exit code: 0 success, 1 usage, 2 system, 3 gate failed, 4 refused.

Advice.description:
One advice entry: a level, a short kebab-case `type` for programs to match
on, a message, and optionally the one command that follows it up.

command.description: The command that acts on this advice, if any.

message.description: One line for people. For `next`, the command itself.

AdviceLevel.description: How much an advice entry matters.

oneOf.description: Something to know or do next.
Something failed (a gate, a partial batch).

CsrfEditUsed.description: A CSRF token a send replaced: where, by name, never the value.

name.description: The name as the request wrote it.

CsrfUsed.description:
What CSRF tracking did in a send (bn-1143); null in a result when it did
nothing. Never a token value.

fetched.description: The source page flow fetched first, if one was.

note.description:
`unknown-source` or `not-refreshed` when a token could not be
refreshed.

FlowReplayed.description:
`flows replay`: the replay of a flow (plan 7.3), or with `--dry-run` what
it would send.

csrf.description: What CSRF tracking did (bn-1143); null when nothing.

diff.description:
The new flow against its parent; null when it could not be read back
(capture off, or not yet committed).

ended_by.description:
The refusal that ended `--times` before the last copy, or the next
redirect hop before it was sent; null when nothing was refused.

flows.description:
Every flow the replay created, in order: the replay, its redirect
hops, then each further copy.

id.description: The new flow's ID; null with `--dry-run` or when capture is off.

length.description: Its response body bytes; null without a response.

macro_replay.description:
With `--macro`: the steps that ran before and the step replayed
(`flows` is then empty: the step's flow is in `macro_replay`); null
otherwise.

notes.description:
What the edits did that the flow should say (a body decoded to be
edited and sent uncompressed, a field added).

parent.description:
The replayed flow (what `flow` resolved to); 0 with `--macro`, which
replays a macro step and no flow.

plan.description: With `--dry-run`, everything the send would check.

relogin.description:
bn-k64x: what was done about a logged-out answer (a login, a retry,
a pause); null when no answer was logged-out.

session.description:
The session it was sent as and where that choice came from
(`--session`, the project default, or none).

status.description: The response status of the new flow; null without one.

text.description:
The result as text for people: one `ID  status  length  time` line
per flow, or the dry run. May hold captured bytes; the CLI escapes it.

time_ms.description: Its time in milliseconds; null with `--dry-run`.

withheld.description:
Header names the session's origin rule kept off the request (never
values); null when nothing was held back.

MacroReplay.description:
What `--macro NAME --step N` ran: the preparatory steps and the step
itself (bn-wyh7). Names, statuses and lengths; never a value of a
variable, a cookie, a token or a secret.

job.description:
The job: kind `replay-macro`, settings `{macro, step, session}`; null
with `--dry-run`.

preparatory.description:
The preparatory steps `1..step`, in order: each ran fresh (with
`--dry-run`: would run, outcome `planned`).

replaced.description:
The substitutions of the step (their locations) that an edit of this
call replaced: the edit wins for the location it names.

replayed.description:
The step itself after the edits (with `--dry-run`: outcome
`planned`).

state_changing.description: The steps among `1..=step` that change state on the target.

units.description:
Units the call spent (with `--dry-run`: needs): one per step sent, so
`step`.

units_left.description: Units of the pass's `requests` ceiling left; null when not metered.

variables.description: The variables the preparatory steps bound, names and lengths.

ReloginUsed.description:
bn-k64x: what the session sender did about a logged-out answer; null in
a result when no answer was logged-out. Names, words and flow IDs only,
never a cookie or secret value.

action.description:
What was done: `re-logged-in` (this send ran the login),
`login-shared` (another send's login, or one already done since this
request went, gave the new cookies), `login-failed` (the login ran
and did not finish; the session is paused when its answers showed
it), `login-stopped` (a stop or a refusal cut the login: nothing is
paused), `paused` (logged out again straight after a login, or in a
job with no login macro), `reported` (no login macro, or none that
can run, outside a job: nothing was done).

generation.description: The session's login generation after it (each login adds one).

logged_out_flow.description: The flow whose answer matched the session's logged-out rule.

login.description: The session's login macro, when it has one.

login_flows.description: The flows of the login's steps, in order, when this send ran it.

login_job.description:
The job the login ran in (the caller's, or one of kind `relogin`
for a send outside a job).

not_retried.description:
Why it was not sent again: `state-changing` (only `GET` and `HEAD`
are), `times` (`--times N`), `retried-once`, `login-failed`,
`login-stopped`, `paused`, `no-login`.

paused.description: True when the session is paused now.

ran.description: True when this send ran the login.

reason.description: The reason word of a login that did not finish.

retried.description: True when the request was sent again with the new cookies.

retry_flow.description: The flow of that second send.

rule.description: The rule that matched, as written.

ReplayDiff.description:
The diff summary of a replay against its parent (plan 7.3): the
`summary` of `flows diff`, cut to what decides whether to look closer.

body_similarity.description:
Similarity of the response bodies, 0 to 1; 1 only for identical
decoded content.

identical.description: Everything compared equal and nothing was undetermined.

status.description: `same` or `changed`: the response status against the parent's.

ReplayPlan.description:
What `--dry-run` found: the request and the scope verdict; nothing sent,
nothing counted.

not_checked.description:
What the dry run did not check: the pass (names and addresses), the
window and the stop, which a send checks before it dials.

raw.description: True for `--as-sent` and `--raw-file`: the bytes go uncorrected.

request.description:
The request that would be written (head and body), lossy UTF-8.
Captured bytes.

units_left.description:
Units left of the ceiling as last read (nothing is reserved); null
when nothing is metered (no pass, or no `requests` ceiling).

units_needed.description:
Units of the pass's `requests` ceiling the send needs: one per
request, `--times` copies (a followed redirect needs one more each).

would_refuse.description:
Scope's refusal (every name the request carries, the destination and
the path); null when scope allows it.

ReplayedFlow.description:
One flow a replay created: the replay itself, a further copy of
`--times`, or a redirect hop of `--follow`.

id.description: The new flow's ID; null when capture is off (it was still sent).

kind.description:
`replay` (the first), `repeat` (a further copy of `--times`) or
`redirect` (a hop `--follow` took).

length.description: Response body bytes; null without a response.

location.description: A redirect's `Location`, as the server sent it. Server data.

outcome.description:
`complete` (the whole response was read), `unknown` (bytes were
written but no complete response came: the server may have acted,
and it was not sent again) or `stopped` (a stop cut it).

parent.description:
The flow it derives from: the replayed flow, or for a redirect hop
the hop before it.

status.description: The response status; null without a response.

time_ms.description: Milliseconds from the connection's start to the end of the exchange.

SessionSource.description: Where a sending command's session came from.

oneOf.description: Neither: the request went without a session.

SessionUsed.description:
The session a send used and why: in every result of a command that
sends (`session: { name, source }`). Never a value.

name.description:
The session's name, `anon` for `--session anon`; null when the
request went with no session.

class.description:
The response class: `2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`, `1xx`, or `blocked`
(a challenge); null without a response.

csrf_refreshed.description:
Names of the CSRF tokens the session's tracking replaced in this
step's request (names only; empty when none).

flow.description:
The flow recorded for it; null when nothing was sent or capture is
off.

outcome.description:
`complete` (sent and answered), `unknown` (written, no complete
answer), `stopped` (a stop cut it), `refused` (not sent: a refusal or
a failure before sending), `failed` (sent, then its extraction or
check failed), `planned` (`--dry-run`) or `not-run` (after the step
that ended the run, or past `--until`).

reason.description: Why it did not complete, as a reason word; null otherwise.

references.description:
The references it used, by name, each once (`{{csrf}}`,
`{{secret:alice.password}}`).

set.description: The variables it set, in order.

state_changing.description: The step changes state on the target.

status.description: The response status; null without one.

url.description:
The URL as written in the file, references by name. Text from a
file: escaped before it reaches a terminal.

withheld.description:
Header names the session's origin rule kept off this step's request
(names only; empty when none).

VariableSet.description:
A variable a step set: its name and the length of its value. Never the
value.

by.description:
`extract` (an extract rule of this step) or `compute` (this step's
compute command).

WithheldHeaders.description: What the session's origin rule kept off the request: names, never values.

names.description:
The header names (and `{{secret}}` carriers) that were left off at
least one request of the send.

reason.description:
Always `session-origin`: the destination is not one of the session's
origins.

WouldRefuse.description: Why scope would refuse a send, as `--dry-run` reports it.

fix.description: The command that fixes it (`teapot scope add HOST`).
